summary: ansible.builtin modules assume UTF-8 text, so on z/OS you must check encodings and configure the remote environment first. The command and shell modules may get EBCDIC or untagged UTF-8 output that gets mis-converted, which you can fix by piping output through iconv.
questions: Why is the output of my shell task on z/OS garbled?
Do I need special setup before using builtin modules on z/OS?
How do I convert command output encoding on z/OS in a shell task?
Can the z/OS shell return EBCDIC output to Ansible?

answer_card.title: Using command and shell modules on z/OS UNIX
answer_card.answer_md:
`ansible.builtin` modules assume all text is UTF-8; on z/OS it may be EBCDIC or UTF-8, so check the encoding of your data. First configure the remote environment (the LE environment variables).

With `command`/`shell`, `/bin/sh` may return EBCDIC. Tagged streams are converted correctly, but a program that returns untagged UTF-8 may be wrongly converted and become unreadable. If you know the source encoding, pipe through `iconv` in a shell task, for example `some_pgm | iconv -f ibm-1047 -t iso8859-1` (adjust the encodings to your files).
